shipped_originals.title_o: Female facial attractiveness increases during the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle
shipped_originals.authors_o: Roberts; Havlicek; Flegr; Hruskova; Little; Jones; Perrett; Petrie

blind_target.title: Changes in fat distribution (WHR) and body weight across the menstrual cycle.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The objective of the current research was to provide an operational replication of the finding that women’s faces are more attractive at high fertility (Roberts et al., 2004) and of the finding that women’s WHRs are lower at high fertility (Kirchengast and Gartner, 2002).
blind_target.outcome_quote: We designed the current study to replicate two other potential cues of women’s ovulatory status: lower waist-to-hip ratios at high fertility and enhanced facial attractiveness at high fertility. We failed to replicate either effect.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict for both designated replication targets.

shipped_originals.title_o: The effects of reading material on social and non-social cognition

blind_target.authors: Hall, A. E., & Bracken, C. C.
blind_target.title: “I really liked that movie”: Testing the relationship between trait empathy, transportation, perceived realism, and movie enjoyment.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The first hypothesis was that trait empathy would be positively correlated with narrative transportation (Hall & Bracken, 2011; Taylor, 2015).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The correlation detected between trait empathy and narrative transportation supports and extends prior literature that has demonstrated similar results with films (Hall & Bracken, 2011; Taylor, 2015), as well as studies that have examined the relationship between some components of trait empathy and narrative transportation into written pieces (Bal & Veltkamp, 2013; Johnson, 2012).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit discussion comparison settles this published finding.
